g.data-info: The bone of the jaw that forms the sockets holding the roots of the teeth.
Fibres of connective tissue that attach the cementum of the root to the jaw bone, cushioning the tooth when chewing.
Soft tissue covering the jaw bone and fitting tightly around the neck of the tooth.
A thin layer of bone-like tissue covering the root that anchors the periodontal ligament fibres.
Hard, yellowish living tissue forming most of the tooth, slightly softer than enamel and containing fine tubules.
The hardest substance in the body, a non-living layer covering the crown that resists wear.
The soft centre of the tooth containing pulp with blood vessels and nerves that keep the tooth alive.
A narrow channel running through each root, connecting the pulp cavity to the jaw at the root tip.
Blood vessels and a nerve enter the root tip to supply the pulp with nutrients and detect pain and temperature.
The part of the tooth visible above the gum, covered with enamel.
The narrow region where the crown meets the root, at the gum line.
The part of the tooth embedded in the jaw bone, anchoring it in place.
